# NaN test vectors

`nan.tsv` holds NaN encodings for tokenator-edn's float tests
(`crates/tokenator-edn/tests/nan_vectors.rs`).

- **Source:** draft-bormann-cbor-numbers-03 (C. Bormann, March 2026),
  Appendix B.1.3 "NaN Tests Examples", Table 2 "Examples for Preferred
  Serialization of NaN values":
  <https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-bormann-cbor-numbers-03.html#name-nan-tests-examples>.
  These are the 10 rows marked `table2`. The `ieee` and `preferred` columns
  are copied from the table.
- **Derived rows** (marked `derived: …`) were added for this project:
  - each Table 2 value with the sign bit flipped;
  - extra binary16, binary32, and binary64 NaNs: signaling NaNs, the
    smallest payloads, and payloads that narrow only part of the way.
  Their `preferred` column follows the same rule as Table 2: narrow only
  when no payload bit is lost (draft §B.1.2).
- **`input`** is the IEEE value encoded at its own width (`f9`/`fa`/`fb`).
- **`edn_input` / `edn_preferred`** are the EDN the tokenator-edn printer
  must produce for those bytes:
  - `NaN` for the canonical quiet NaN (`f9 7e00`);
  - otherwise `float'…'` with the shortest exact bytes
    (draft-ietf-cbor-edn-literals-28 §3.7);
  - plus `_1`/`_2`/`_3` when the encoding is wider than preferred.

The file was generated by a short script from the Table 2 rows and checked
against them. Lines starting with `#` are comments; the first other line is
the header.
